answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
First find the least number exactly divisible by 8, 14, 20 and 25, that is their LCM.
\(8 = 2^3\), \(14 = 2 \times 7\), \(20 = 2^2 \times 5\), \(25 = 5^2\)
LCM \(= 2^3 \times 5^2 \times 7 = 8 \times 25 \times 7 = 1400\)
The number must leave remainder 4 in each case, so add 4.
Required number \(= 1400 + 4 = 1404\)
So, the answer is 1404.

answers.label: Q2
answers.solution:
Let the cost price be \(C\) dollars.
Original selling price (gain \(5\%\)) \(= \frac{105}{100}C\)
New selling price (loss \(5\%\)) \(= \frac{95}{100}C\)
The difference is the 50 dollars reduction:
\(\frac{105}{100}C - \frac{95}{100}C = 50\)
\(\frac{10}{100}C = 50\), so \(C = 500\) dollars.
Original selling price \(= \frac{105}{100} \times 500 = 525\) dollars.
So, the original selling price is 525 dollars.

answers.label: Q5
answers.solution:
Note: as printed the question cannot work. Dividing by \(\frac{4}{5}\) is the same as multiplying by \(\frac{5}{4}\), so the two answers would be equal and could not differ by 36. The sensible reading is: he was asked to multiply the number by \(\frac{4}{5}\) but divided it by \(\frac{4}{5}\).
Let the number be \(x\).
Correct answer \(= \frac{4}{5}x\)
Wrong answer \(= x \div \frac{4}{5} = \frac{5}{4}x\)
\(\frac{5}{4}x - \frac{4}{5}x = 36\)
\(\frac{25x - 16x}{20} = 36\)
\(\frac{9x}{20} = 36\), so \(x = \frac{36 \times 20}{9} = 80\)
So, the given number is 80.

Let the selling price of 1 m be \(s\).
SP of 33 m \(= 33s\); profit \(= 11s\)
CP of 33 m \(= \text{SP} - \text{Profit} = 33s - 11s = 22s\)
Profit \(\% = \frac{11s}{22s} \times 100 = 50\%\)
So, the profit percentage is \(50\%\).

Each exterior angle of the first polygon \(= 180^\circ - 144^\circ = 36^\circ\)
Number of sides \(= \frac{360^\circ}{36^\circ} = 10\)
The second polygon has \(2 \times 10 = 20\) sides.
Each exterior angle \(= \frac{360^\circ}{20} = 18^\circ\)
Each interior angle \(= 180^\circ - 18^\circ = 162^\circ\)
So, the interior angle of the second polygon is \(162^\circ\).

answers.label: Q9
answers.solution:
Side of the square \(= \sqrt{16} = 4\) cm.
Each mid-point is 2 cm from a corner. A side of the inner square joins two mid-points of adjacent sides, so by Pythagoras it is \(\sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{8}\) cm.
Area of the inner square \(= (\sqrt{8})^2 = 8\text{ cm}^2\)
(The square joining the mid-points always has half the area of the original square: \(\frac{16}{2} = 8\).)
So, the area is \(8\text{ cm}^2\).

answers.label: Q10
answers.solution:
Note: as printed, \(12x^2 - 17xy + 26y^2\) has no factors: we need two numbers with product \(12 \times 26 = 312\) and sum \(-17\), and none exist. The last term is most likely \(6y^2\), which is solved below.
\(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2\)
Product \(12 \times 6 = 72\), sum \(-17\): the numbers are \(-9\) and \(-8\).
\(= 12x^2 - 9xy - 8xy + 6y^2\)
\(= 3x(4x - 3y) - 2y(4x - 3y)\)
\(= (3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\)
So, the factors are \((3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\).

answers.label: Q11
answers.solution:
\(x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2) = (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2)\)
So \(\frac{x^4 - y^4}{x - y} = (x + y)(x^2 + y^2)\)
\(= x^3 + xy^2 + x^2y + y^3\)
So, the quotient is \(x^3 + x^2y + xy^2 + y^3\) and the remainder is 0.

answers.solution:
In triangle PQR, \(\angle R = 40^\circ\) and \(\angle Q = 40^\circ\).
\(\angle P = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = 100^\circ\)
PR is parallel to ST and PS (part of PQ) is a transversal. \(\angle RPS\) and \(\angle PST\) (which is \(x\)) are co-interior angles, so they add up to \(180^\circ\).
\(x = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ\)
(Check: \(\angle QST = \angle QPR = 100^\circ\) as corresponding angles, and \(x + 100^\circ = 180^\circ\) on the straight line PQ.)
So, \(x = 80^\circ\).

The figure is a regular pentagon, so each side is \(\frac{1}{5} = \frac{5}{25}\) of the periphery.
Starting from the top vertex S and going clockwise, the sides come in the order H, B, C, D, E.
After side H: \(\frac{5}{25}\); after B: \(\frac{10}{25}\); after C: \(\frac{15}{25}\); after D: \(\frac{20}{25}\).
\(\frac{18}{25}\) lies between \(\frac{15}{25}\) and \(\frac{20}{25}\), so the cat is on the fourth side, D (it has walked \(\frac{3}{25}\) of the periphery, that is \(\frac{3}{5}\) of side D, along it).
So, the cat reaches side D.

answers.label: Q15
answers.solution:
The four large circles touch each other, so their centres form a square of side \(r + r = 2r\).
Diagonal of this square \(= 2r\sqrt{2}\); half the diagonal \(= r\sqrt{2}\).
The small circle sits at the centre of the square and touches all four circles, so the distance from a large centre to the middle equals \(r + \rho\), where \(\rho\) is the small radius.
\(r + \rho = r\sqrt{2}\)
\(\rho = r\sqrt{2} - r = (\sqrt{2} - 1)r \approx 0.414r\)
So, the radius of the inner circle is \((\sqrt{2} - 1)r\).

answers.label: Q16
answers.solution:
The father took \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the cake, which is 3 times what each other member had.
Share of each other member \(= \frac{1}{4} \div 3 = \frac{1}{12}\)
Cake left for the others \(= 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\)
Number of other members \(= \frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{4} \times 12 = 9\)
Total members \(= 9 + 1 = 10\)
So, the family has 10 members.

Every term has the common factor \((x + y)\).
\((a+b)(x+y) + (2a+3)(x+y) - (3a+4b)(x+y)\)
\(= (x + y)[(a + b) + (2a + 3) - (3a + 4b)]\)
\(= (x + y)[a + b + 2a + 3 - 3a - 4b]\)
\(= (x + y)(3 - 3b)\)
\(= 3(x + y)(1 - b)\)
So, the expression factorises as \(3(x + y)(1 - b)\).

answers.label: Q21
answers.solution:
Remove the bar (vinculum) first: \(3x - \overline{2x - y} = 3x - 2x + y = x + y\).
The expression becomes \(23x - [15y - \{4y - 2(3x - 2y) - 3(x + y)\}]\).
Open the small brackets:
\(-2(3x - 2y) = -6x + 4y\) and \(-3(x + y) = -3x - 3y\)
Curly bracket: \(\{4y - 6x + 4y - 3x - 3y\} = \{5y - 9x\}\)
Square bracket: \([15y - (5y - 9x)] = [15y - 5y + 9x] = [10y + 9x]\)
Finally: \(23x - (10y + 9x) = 23x - 10y - 9x = 14x - 10y\)
So, the expression simplifies to \(14x - 10y\).

The new cube has the same volume, so its edge \(= \sqrt[3]{216} = 6\) cm.

answers.label: Q23
answers.solution:
(a) Note: as printed, the powers are \(m+n\), \(m+k\), \(k+n\). The question asks for a value, and the well-known form of this question has powers \(m+n\), \(n+k\), \(k+m\) (each bracket raised to the sum of its own two letters). Read that way:
\(\left(x^{m-n}\right)^{m+n} \left(x^{n-k}\right)^{n+k} \left(x^{k-m}\right)^{k+m}\)
\(= x^{m^2 - n^2} \cdot x^{n^2 - k^2} \cdot x^{k^2 - m^2}\)
\(= x^{m^2 - n^2 + n^2 - k^2 + k^2 - m^2} = x^0 = 1\)
(Taken exactly as printed, the power adds up to \((m-n)(m+n) + (n-k)(m+k) + (k-m)(k+n) = (m-n)(m+n-2k)\), giving \(x^{(m-n)(m+n-2k)}\), which is not a fixed value.)

(b) Let \(a = x^{m-n}\). Then \(x^{n-m} = \frac{1}{a}\).
\(\frac{1}{1 + a} + \frac{1}{1 + \frac{1}{a}} = \frac{1}{1 + a} + \frac{a}{a + 1} = \frac{1 + a}{1 + a} = 1\)
So, the answers are (a) 1 and (b) 1.

answers.solution:
Let the first part be ₹ \(x\); the second part is ₹ \((1200 - x)\).
SI on first part \(= \frac{x \times 6 \times 2}{100} = \frac{12x}{100}\)
SI on second part \(= \frac{(1200 - x) \times 8 \times 3}{100} = \frac{24(1200 - x)}{100}\)
They are equal:
\(12x = 24(1200 - x)\)
\(x = 2(1200 - x) = 2400 - 2x\)
\(3x = 2400\), so \(x = 800\)
Second part \(= 1200 - 800 = 400\)
(Check: SI \(= 96\) on both.)
So, the two parts are ₹ 800 and ₹ 400.

answers.label: Q25
answers.solution:
First three-fourth of the journey \(= \frac{3}{4} \times 360 = 270\) km.
Time taken \(= \frac{270}{60} = 4\frac{1}{2}\) hours.
Remaining distance \(= 360 - 270 = 90\) km.
Remaining time \(= 5\frac{3}{4} - 4\frac{1}{2} = 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\) hours.
Speed \(= 90 \div \frac{5}{4} = 90 \times \frac{4}{5} = 72\) km/hr
So, the speed for the rest of the journey is 72 km/hr.

Product of extremes = product of means:
\((3 + x)(19 + x) = (5 + x)(13 + x)\)

\(4x = 8\), so \(x = 2\)

answers.label: Q27
answers.finalAnswer: 60 marks; 60 marks; Hindi; Science; Mathematics and Social Science
answers.solution:
Note: the pie chart prints Social Science as \(5^\circ\), but the angles must total \(360^\circ\): \(360^\circ - (90^\circ + 55^\circ + 70^\circ + 80^\circ) = 65^\circ\). So Social Science is \(65^\circ\) (the 6 is missing in print).
Marks for each subject \(= \frac{\text{angle}}{360^\circ} \times 540 = \text{angle} \times 1.5\)
Mathematics \(= 90 \times 1.5 = 135\); English \(= 55 \times 1.5 = 82.5\); Hindi \(= 70 \times 1.5 = 105\); Science \(= 80 \times 1.5 = 120\); Social Science \(= 65 \times 1.5 = 97.5\).
(i) English + Science + Social Science \(= 82.5 + 120 + 97.5 = 300\); Hindi + Mathematics \(= 105 + 135 = 240\). Excess \(= 300 - 240 = 60\) marks.
(ii) Hindi + Mathematics \(= 240\); English + Social Science \(= 82.5 + 97.5 = 180\). Excess \(= 240 - 180 = 60\) marks.
(iii) 105 marks is Hindi.
(iv) \(22.2\%\) of \(360^\circ \approx 80^\circ\) (\(\frac{80}{360} = 22.2\%\)), which is Science.
(v) English and Science differ by \(80^\circ - 55^\circ = 25^\circ\) (37.5 marks). Mathematics and Social Science also differ by \(90^\circ - 65^\circ = 25^\circ\).
So, the answers are: (i) 60 marks, (ii) 60 marks, (iii) Hindi, (iv) Science, (v) Mathematics and Social Science.

Selling price after \(10\%\) discount \(= 90\%\) of M.P. \(= ₹\ 540\)
M.P. \(= \frac{540 \times 100}{90} = ₹\ 600\)
Without discount he sells at ₹ 600 and makes a \(20\%\) profit:

answers.label: Q30
answers.solution:
The three slanting lines (with arrows) are parallel, and the two long lines are transversals cutting them. The figure is not drawn to scale, so use the given angles.
Transversal rising to the right (it makes \(70^\circ\) with the right parallel line):
\(a = 70^\circ\) (corresponding angle to the \(70^\circ\) angle).
\(b = 180^\circ - a = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ\) (angles on a straight line).
\(d = 70^\circ\): the angle at the left parallel line corresponding to \(70^\circ\) lies above the transversal on the right, and \(d\) is vertically opposite to it.
Transversal falling to the right (it makes \(112^\circ\) with the left parallel line):
\(e = 112^\circ\) (corresponding angle to the \(112^\circ\) angle at the right parallel line).
\(c = 180^\circ - 112^\circ = 68^\circ\) (\(c\) and \(e\) together make a straight angle on that transversal).
So, \(a = 70^\circ\), \(b = 110^\circ\), \(c = 68^\circ\), \(d = 70^\circ\), \(e = 112^\circ\).
